title: Library Catalog
story: Books line the shelves: 'Dune', 'Foundation', 'Neuromancer'. Patrons borrow and return them. You need to track: who has what, what's available, and when things are due. Build a library catalog — a mini database with search, checkout, and return operations.
why: The library catalog combines structs for books, enums for status, Vec for catalog, Option for search results, and CRUD operations — a complete information management system.
analogy: A library card catalog (the old wooden cabinet with tiny drawers). Each card = a book. Flip through to find what you want. Your digital catalog is searchable, sortable, and tracks not just what's in the library but WHO has each book. No Dewey Decimal required.
try_it: Add due date tracking: checkout sets due_date to 14 days from now. Add overdue detection. Implement search by title (partial match) and author. Add book categories/genres. Track checkout history per book.
tips: Use enums for book status — clearer than booleans (Available/CheckedOut vs true/false)
Return Option[Book] for search results — None means 'not found'
In-place update: find book by index, replace entire struct with updated fields
common_mistakes: Not checking status before checkout — available book only
Not checking status before return — already-available books can't be returned
Searching linearly for every operation — consider Map by ID for O(1) lookups
